mainEntity.name: What is another name for par-level inventory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Par is also called the order-up-to level or the max level. Whatever the name, it is the stock a line should hold right after a delivery lands: 1,080 cases on these defaults.

mainEntity.name: What is the par level formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: Average daily usage times the days you have to cover, where those days are your delivery cycle plus your buffer. Here that is 120 x 9, so 1,080 cases. The par level calculation rounds up to whole cases, and today's order is par less whatever the count says is on the floor.

mainEntity.name: How is a par level different from a reorder point?

acceptedAnswer.text: A par level answers how much, and a reorder point answers when. Par here is 1,080 cases, the level the next delivery brings this line back to. A reorder point is a level on the way down that says place the order now. On a line that matters you want both numbers, and they are two separate calculations.

mainEntity.name: How many buffer days should a par level carry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Price the day before you pick it. One buffer day on this line is $2,640 of stock, so 2 days is $5,280 sitting there for a supplier who misses dates. On a supplier who unloads on the promised day, carry one day or none and put the $2,640 somewhere it earns.

mainEntity.name: How much cash does a par level tie up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply par by your landed case cost. 1,080 cases at $22.00 is $23,760 on the floor at the top of every cycle. Take out one buffer day and par falls to 960 cases, which is $21,120, so the day you were carrying was worth $2,640 of working capital.

mainEntity.name: How do you work out how much to order up to par?

acceptedAnswer.text: Subtract today's count from par. 1,080 par less 340 cases on hand is a 740 case order, $16,280 at $22.00 a case. If the count comes in over par, the calculator names how many cases you are carrying above the level instead of sizing an order.

mainEntity.name: How often should you reset your par levels?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whenever usage or the delivery cycle moves, and on a quarterly sweep otherwise. Going from a weekly drop to a 3 day route takes this par level from 1,080 cases to 600 and the cash at par from $23,760 to $13,200. A par level definition set last spring is still priced at last spring's case cost.
